156: ### R6 — Grapheme: separate policy/kernel from optional authoring/runtime activation (design now, packaging later; M/L)

158: **Evidence / confidence:** High static facts; medium packaging proposal; no claimed runtime saving. Default `full-daemon` pulls `stasis-rs/grapheme-full` (`Cargo.toml:235-251`) and direct optional compiler/runtime/LSP deps (`:139-143,292-295`); `embedded-daemon` uses `grapheme-host` (`:327-348`). Bridge dependency registration occurs in Stasis wiring (`src/runtime/stasis_wire.rs:142-146`). But workflow engine construction is already a lazy OnceLock (`src/grapheme_medousa_bridge.rs:145-147`) and workshop session separately lazy (`src/grapheme_workshop.rs:16-31`). “Everything loads at boot” is not supported by these facts.

160: **Proposed responsibility/interface:** A small `GraphemeExecutionPort` exposed through existing workflow/tool surfaces, carrying source/run identity, policy context, secret scope, cancellation, and durable result identity; optional authoring/hotload capability reports compiler/workshop availability. Treat shared policy configuration as immutable process/workshop policy with explicit version, not arbitrary first request wins. Keep tool/capability discovery cheap and available even if compiler/runtime not activated yet. Preserve normal installation functionality; optional activation is not feature removal.

162: **What must remain daemon-owned:** admission/authorization; allowlist and schedule preflight; durable job identity/idempotency; run-scoped secrets, filesystem/network/shell host capabilities; budgets/cancellation; receipts and terminal barriers. What may be optional/lazy: authoring compiler/LSP, workshop hotload session, module discovery enrichment and expensive interpreter resources if first-use behavior remains honest. Do not lazily defer required store/recovery/grant readiness. The external Grapheme CLI path (`src/tools.rs:74-81`) must not become a bypass when in-process support is unavailable.

166: **Risk/blast:** High security/scheduling/feature matrix; secrets cannot migrate into persisted script state. Cancellation does not imply interpreter abort. Current bridge explicitly joins the blocking interpreter after requesting cancellation (`src/grapheme_medousa_bridge.rs:268-327`); retain this honesty.

168: **Tests/gates:** Existing preflight and job tests `src/grapheme_runtime.rs:435,469,487,504,526,594,619,647` cover queue contention, compile-without-execution, another worker claiming, waiter timeout/drop, receipt persistence and retry receipt identity. Add unavailable-compiler capability result; concurrent lazy first use; module isolation between workshop/workflow; allowlist change behavior; expired/foreign secret scope; cancelled shell host; unavailable CLI cannot execute unapproved source. Compare same source/result and durable job semantics with eager baseline.

The strongest source-level candidates are watcher burst amplification, full-history prompt preparation, and messaging connection/schema churn. They are not measured production bottlenecks.

107: ## Grapheme: separate catalog, compilation, execution and residency

109: - `src/grapheme_host_catalog.rs:1–8`, `:112`: discovery uses a static manifest catalog, explicitly distinct from runtime WASM loading. `src/grapheme_api.rs:44–79` builds list summaries and serializes effect/ABI enum values on request. There is an allocation/caching opportunity if discovery is frequent, **not** evidence that listing runs all modules.

110: - `src/grapheme_workshop.rs:16–31`: workshop engine/session are process-global `OnceLock<Mutex<_>>`, initialized on first workshop-session use. This intentionally retains state until process exit and serializes mutations. Measure first use separately from steady state; a lock-free replacement could break lifecycle/hot-load semantics.

111: - `src/grapheme_medousa_bridge.rs:132–148`: workflow engine is already process-global/lazy; code explicitly avoids rebuilding host registration/hotload/interceptors per execution. Preserve per-call state seeds and guardrails. Do not propose this already-existing optimization as new work.

112: - `src/grapheme_runtime.rs` exposes compile/inspect/execute and runtime module operations. Source validation, compilation, allowed-module checks and effect-time authorization are distinct responsibilities. If duplicate parse/compile dominates, cache immutable artifacts by source digest **plus** compiler/ABI/guardrail/module versions, not a previous authorization result. This remains a hypothesis, not a prioritized proven bottleneck.

113: - Runtime Grapheme execution is not merely in-process function dispatch: `src/grapheme_runtime.rs:30–54` enqueues a durable job and waits for its own matching terminal attempt receipt. See the polling finding below. This explains possible tool/job overhead separately from module loading.
170: ### P2 — Measure Grapheme job-result polling and shared queue driving

172: **Source/confidence:** high for behavior, unmeasured workload frequency. `src/grapheme_runtime.rs:56–151`: waiter polls `get_job` and `list_job_attempts` with a 50 ms sleep interval and 60 s budget. While its job is enqueued it can launch a shared-queue `process_once` pass, which may execute unrelated work. A pass is deliberately not aborted when the waiter is dropped. Multiple simultaneous waiters can therefore add repeated DB observations/queue-driving alongside normal workers. This is not proof of duplicate execution: durable leases/attempt matching remain authoritative.

198: **Verification/rollback:** fresh and seeded fixture stores, stage timestamps, process-to-serving/chat-ready p50/p95, first and second Grapheme/Detamu use and RSS. Test interrupted work cannot execute before authority recovery. Revert deferral/readiness changes per domain; do not roll back migrated durable data without compatible readers.

213: 3. **Cases.** (a) empty/seeded startup, (b) short/long transcript prompt-ready and stub first token, (c) no-op tool with policy success/denial, (d) isolated mailbox send/retry/restart, (e) Forge metadata/observation under watcher burst, (f) synthetic stream append/replay/terminal, (g) workspace mutation/checkpoint burst. Seed 10/1k/10k transcript entries; keep initial payload totals under 32 MiB and state exact sizes.
